endorsements.quote: Performance should be reported separately by subgroup rather than only in aggregate, following the same logic the FDA has proposed for pulse oximetry12, and should report calibration alongside discrimination (sensitivity and specificity), since a model can retain apparent sensitivity while systematically over- or under-estimating malignancy risk within a subgroup.

Because most patients contribute multiple images and because subgroup sample sizes are often small, these studies should pre-specify adequate sample sizes or a minimum detectable effect via a power calculation, report confidence intervals around every subgroup estimate, use patient-level clustering (for example, mixed-effects or generalized estimating equation models rather than naive image-level confidence intervals) to avoid overstating precision, and formally test for a pigmentation-by-outcome interaction rather than relying on eyeballing separate subgroup point estimates.

Third, algorithm developers and journals publishing validation studies should require subgroup-stratified sensitivity, specificity, and calibration reporting as a condition of publication, in the same way subgroup reporting has become standard practice in dermatology AI evaluation following that field’s own reckoning with this issue, and should report against established AI-specific reporting frameworks such as STARD-AI for diagnostic accuracy studies26 and TRIPOD + AI for studies developing or validating a prediction model27, both of which now explicitly ask authors to address fairness and subgroup performance in their methods and discussion.
External validation on a genuinely held-out population, not a re- split of the same source cohorts, should be treated as a minimum bar before a claim of generalizability is made.

Operationally, this could take the form of a structured pre-deployment checklist item requiring documented, subgroup-stratified validation evidence, or an explicit acknowledgment of its absence, before an implementation team proceeds to workforce training and workflow design.

unlisted_practices: Validate AI-assisted oral screening classifiers prospectively for performance variation by physiologic oral pigmentation, stratified by anatomical site, before deployment in a new population.

Capture site-specific, quantitative measures of oral mucosal pigmentation in training and validation datasets, not only self-reported race, using standardized image acquisition protocols with calibrated lighting and color-reference cards.
Use multivariable models and controlled reader studies to separate pigmentation effects from other sources of dataset shift such as device, site, lesion type, and acquisition protocol.
Funders should treat population-specific validation as a required, fundable component of AI screening implementation research.
Incorporate algorithmic generalizability and equity readiness as determinants in implementation science frameworks such as CFIR.
